For patients with double prosthetic valves who have developed prosthetic valve endocarditis, surgical treatment options are available. A single-valve replacement may be a viable option for these patients.

This approach is safe when guided by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) to confirm site involvement and correlation with the anatomic diagnosis obtained during surgery. Single-valve replacement can provide similar benefits to two-ventricle replacement, including improved symptom relief and quality of life, while potentially reducing complications related to prosthetic valve endocarditis.

However, it's essential to consider factors such as patient age, overall health status, and comorbidities when deciding on the most suitable surgical approach. In elderly patients (at least 75 years old), two-ventricle replacement is often preferred due to reduced long-term survival rates and quality of life.

In conclusion, while single-valve replacement can be a safe option for patients with double prosthetic valves who have developed endocarditis, it's crucial to weigh the benefits against potential risks and consider individual patient factors before making an informed decision.
